summary: Mars Map is a prototype solution for the Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map that helps future explorers plan journeys across Mars. Our demonstration focuses on Gale Crater, we combined NASA and USGS terrain data with environmental models to calculate routes that account for steep slopes, rough terrain, estimated radiation exposure, and dust-related surface conditions.  Users select a stating point and destination, then view the proposed route with its estimated distance and walking time. We used numbered markers to explain important detours, which helped make the route's reasoning easier to understand. Mars Map is designed for a wrist-mounted device. It helps demonstrate how explainable mapping could help prepare for the human exploration.
details:
Mars Map is an interactive interface prototype that helps users plan and understand proposed routes across the Martian surface. Our demonstration focuses on Gale Crate, where mission data provides a foundation for exploring terrain while being aware of environmental conditions.

Users select a starting point, represented by an astronaut, and a destination. The application uses the A pathfinding algorithm* to search a grid derived from terrain data. It excludes cells that exceed configured slope or elevation limits and evaluates traversable paths using modeled costs. These costs consider factors such as climbing effort, terrain roughness, estimated radiation exposure, communication visibility, and surface conditions. The resulting route appears on the map with estimated distance and walking time.

One key feature we implemented was explaining why a route changes direction. Numbered markers identify important detours. Selecting a marker displays an explanation and highlights the shortcut the algorithm rejected. This helps users understand the tradeoffs behind a route rather than simply following a line.

The project combines NASA and USGS resources, including MOLA–HRSC elevation data and THEMIS-derived thermal inertia data. Elevation supports slope calculations and terrain constraints. Thermal inertia provides a proxy for surface properties, helping the model penalize potentially dusty or loose terrain. Climate temperature is contextual information rather than a spatial temperature-avoidance system.

We developed MarsMap using JavaScript, React, Vite, and Tailwind CSS. OpenLayers and proj4 support the map and Martian coordinate systems, Chart.js supports charts, and Node.js with GeoTIFF tools prepares raster datasets. The current terrain files are stored with the project, reducing dependence on downloading large datasets when the application opens. We also used Figma to explore interface layouts and Pixilart to create some assets.
dataRefs: NASA Mars Odyssey THEMIS: thermal observations and derived surface-property products
projectRefs: Guo et al. — Martian radiation modeling and measurements
